title: Backtracking
subtitle: Algorithmic technique for solving problems recursively by trying to build a solution incrementally.

patterns.title: Choice-Based Backtracking
patterns.subtitle: Generate all possible combinations, subsets, or permutations by making a choice at each step.

solution.headline: Subsets — backtracking over "take it or leave it".
solution.approach: Every prefix of the recursion is itself a valid subset, so the answer is recorded at every node rather than only at the leaves.

solution.headline: Subsets II — sort first, then skip repeated values at the same depth.
solution.approach: Skipping duplicates only when `i > start` still allows a value to be reused at a deeper level, which is what distinguishes [1,2,2] from a duplicate subset.

solution.headline: Combination Sum — unlimited reuse, so recurse on the same index.
solution.approach: Passing `i` (not `i + 1`) is what allows a candidate to repeat; sorting lets the search stop as soon as a candidate overshoots.

solution.headline: Combination Sum II — each number used once, duplicates skipped per level.
Permutations — swap-based backtracking.
solution.approach: Swapping the current position with every later one enumerates all orderings without a used[] array.

solution.headline: Permutations II — sorted input plus a used[] guard against duplicates.
solution.approach: A duplicate may only be placed if its identical predecessor is already in the current permutation, which fixes one canonical order per multiset.

solution.headline: Next Permutation — find the pivot, swap with its successor, reverse the tail.
solution.approach: The suffix after the pivot is non-increasing, so reversing it turns it into the smallest possible arrangement.

solution.headline: Generate Parentheses — backtrack while the prefix stays valid.
solution.approach: An open bracket is allowed while fewer than n are used; a close bracket only while it would not outnumber the open ones.

solution.headline: Palindrome Partitioning — cut after every palindromic prefix.

patterns.title: Constraint-Based Backtracking

solution.headline: N-Queens — backtracking with diagonal sets.
solution.approach: A queen at (row, col) owns the diagonals row - col and row + col, so conflicts are O(1) set lookups instead of a board scan.

solution.headline: N-Queens II — the same search, counting instead of materialising boards.
M-Coloring Problem — backtracking over the nodes.
solution.approach: Colour node by node; a colour is legal when no already-coloured neighbour uses it. Failing fast on the first uncolourable node is the entire pruning.

solution.headline: Knight's Tour — backtracking with Warnsdorff's heuristic.
solution.approach: Plain backtracking stalls even on an 8x8 board. Warnsdorff's rule — always move to the square with the fewest onward moves — finds a tour almost immediately, and the backtracking stays in place as a safety net when the heuristic ties.
